data.description: Inspired by oz-for-oss (https://github.com/warpdotdev/oz-for-oss/blob/main/docs/platform.md): some incoming requests resolve entirely as fixed mutations and should never engage the agent platform at all. oz routes these as non-agent webhook branches (e.g. `announce-ready-issue`, `plan-approved`) — the router decides deterministically and no Oz run is dispatched. DSO has the bottom half of this pattern (deterministic scripts the LLM calls mid-workflow), but is missing the top half: a pre-LLM classifier that recognizes trivial request shapes and shells straight to the appropriate `.claude/scripts/dso …` invocation with zero orchestrator turns. Distinction from existing scripts: scripts remove LLM cost from the *mechanics*; this layer removes LLM cost from the *routing decision itself*. Candidate trivial shapes: 'close ticket X as duplicate of Y' (→ transition + link), 'tag ticket X with Z' (→ tag), 'list open epics' (→ list-epics), 'show ticket X' (→ show). Scope: design where this layer lives (Claude Code hook? pre-skill router?), define the matchable request grammar, pilot with 3-5 high-frequency shapes, measure token savings and error rate vs LLM-mediated path.
data.title: Pre-LLM deterministic routing layer for trivial requests
